messages:
Nora: heads-up: sample-app async client typing started failing after autogen changed enum handling for open enums (we now allow raw str). mypy hits assignment errors inside async iterators.
Alex: can you paste the error?
Nora: sure:
```
src/clients/async_orders.py:52: error: Incompatible types in assignment (expression has type "str | None", variable has type "OrderStatus | None")  [assignment]
Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 15 source files)
```
Priya: ah, this is the generator emitting `Optional[Union[OrderStatus, str]]` for the field. runtime is fine because validator falls back to raw str, but async return type annotations like `AsyncIterator[Order]` make mypy unhappy when downstream code expects `Order.status` to be `OrderStatus | None`.
Yusuf: pyright behaves differently too. Some customers use strict pyright where `Order.status` being `Union[...]` vs `OrderStatus | str` matters. We need a single generator output that plays nicely with both mypy and pyright and doesn't force `from __future__ import annotations` on users.
Alex: two approaches: 1) keep `Optional[Union[OrderStatus, str]]` in generated models (compatible with py3.8+), or 2) emit `Optional[OrderStatus]` but add a separate `raw_status: Optional[str]` field for unknowns. Option 2 keeps a clean typed enum field but is awkward for callers.
Priya: I dislike adding extra fields. Option 1 is more explicit. But for async iterators, mypy sometimes uses inferred usage sites where it narrows types. We should ensure the stub/type-check tests cover async generator consumption patterns so we catch regressions.
Nora: proposal: generator emits `Optional[Union[OrderStatus, str]]`, includes a comment explaining the fallback, and we add a small typing test in sample-app that consumes the async iterator and asserts the type works with both mypy and pyright. Example test snippet:
```
async def test_stream_order_types() -> None:
    async for order in client.stream_orders():
        reveal_type(order.status)  # mypy: reveal_type -> "Optional[Union[OrderStatus, str]]"
        assert isinstance(order.status, (str, OrderStatus, type(None)))
        break
```
Alex: also ensure generated files import `Union`/`Optional` from typing when used. And avoid using PEP 604 unions so we don't force future imports.
Yusuf: add a small note in PR about pyright compatibility. Some teams use `--enable=reportOptionalMemberAccess` etc. Better to call it out.
CI-bot: sample-app/mypy-check failed on branch async-enum-fix-1975009876  https://ci.internal/runs/5350  logs attached.
Priya: I'll update the generator to emit `Optional[Union[EnumName, str]]`, include the pydantic pre-validator that tries to coerce to EnumName and falls back to raw str, and add the async typing test in sample-app.
Nora: please also add a tiny docstring in generated file describing why unknown enum values are preserved. It saves time for downstream debuggers.
Alex: when opening the PR mention that we intentionally avoid `from __future__ import annotations` to not break older code, but link an issue for follow-up if we decide to move to postponed evaluation of annotations.
CI-bot: PR 4328 opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autogen/pull/4328  includes generator change + sample-app async typing test.
CI-bot: PR 4328 CI: mypy/pyright checks passed, unit tests passed. Merged at 1975009950.
Yusuf: thanks folks. after merge I'll run a quick cross-repo typing smoke (quickstart + playground) to be safe.
Nora: resolved on my end. :thumbsup:
